Andy Robertson has emphasized that shoring up Liverpool's defensive performance will be crucial if they are to mount a serious title challenge under new manager Arne Slot during his inaugural campaign at the helm. The Scottish left-back expressed optimism about the early results, noting that the team has managed to keep two consecutive clean sheets in their opening fixtures of the season against Ipswich and Brentford, giving Slot an ideal beginning to his tenure at Anfield. However, Robertson is well aware that a far sterner examination awaits when Liverpool travel to Old Trafford to take on Manchester United, a fixture that traditionally tests every aspect of a team's resilience and composure. Reflecting on the previous campaign, Robertson acknowledged that Liverpool's defensive record was a significant factor in their inability to sustain a genuine title bid. The club shipped 41 goals across 38 Premier League matches last season, finishing in third place behind Manchester City and Arsenal. That tally was seven more than the champions City conceded and a full 12 more than runners-up Arsenal allowed, highlighting a clear gap in defensive solidity between Liverpool and the teams that finished above them. Robertson candidly admitted that even during the period when Liverpool were still considered contenders in the title race, they were giving up more scoring opportunities to opponents than either Arsenal or Manchester City, and he recognized that such a pattern was always likely to catch up with them eventually.

Handle the defensive side of the game better, and Liverpool could find themselves in a much stronger position to compete for the ultimate prize this time around, Robertson suggested. He made it clear that the early promise shown in the first two matches needs to be sustained not just against Manchester United but throughout the entire season, including the many challenging fixtures that will follow after the upcoming international break. The defender stressed the importance of limiting opponents to as few chances as possible, understanding that even the best goalkeepers and defensive units will eventually be punished if they consistently allow too many opportunities. His comments reflect a mature and analytical approach to the game, one that recognizes defensive discipline as the foundation upon which successful title campaigns are built. Robertson's awareness of the statistical shortcomings from last season demonstrates that the squad has been doing its homework and understands exactly where improvements need to be made under Slot's guidance.

Robertson's words carry the weight of experience, having been part of Liverpool teams that have both won the Premier League and fallen short in title races. His message is simple but powerful: if Liverpool can tighten up at the back and reduce the number of chances they concede on a consistent basis, they will give themselves the best possible platform to challenge for the league title. The early signs under Arne Slot have been encouraging, but the true measure of their progress will come in the tougher matches that lie ahead, starting with the daunting visit to Manchester United. The entire squad appears committed to addressing last season's defensive vulnerabilities and turning those lessons into tangible improvements on the pitch this campaign.

P.S. Robertson's focus on defensive improvement highlights a collective awareness within the Liverpool squad that last season's shortcomings at the back ultimately cost them a realistic shot at the title, and rectifying this under Arne Slot's leadership remains their top priority moving forward.
